specification_compliance: Select all passes only the visible (name-filtered) file ids: FolderBrowser.tsx:968 calls selection.selectAll(visibleFileIds), and visibleFileIds comes from nameFilter.files (FolderBrowser.tsx:188-191).
Shift range uses visibleFileIds (FolderBrowser.tsx:633), so hidden rows are skipped.

Pruning is keyed on the debounced filter text (appliedText) through prunedForTextRef, and it is deferred while loading (FolderBrowser.tsx:620-625). A reload under an unchanged filter therefore does not clear the selection.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Clearing the filter (appliedText becomes empty) updates the ref but does not prune. This is the intended behavior, because every row is visible again.

If a reload under an unchanged filter text brings back a selected file whose name no longer matches (for example, it was renamed elsewhere), that file stays selected while hidden, because pruning runs only when the text changes. Under the personal-use threat model this edge case is unlikely.
regression_risks: The prune effect depends on `loading` from useFolderFiles (useFolderFiles.ts:760). For watch-history views `loading` is derived differently. If it can be false while `files` is transiently empty, a text change at that moment would prune against an empty list.
test_coverage: FolderBrowser.selectionFilter.test.tsx covers Select all under the filter, a Shift range across a hidden file, pruning when the filter hides a selected file, preserving the selection on reload under the filter, deferring the prune during a reload, and resetting the anchor after it is hidden (lines 158-214).
